## Technical Corrections to This Historical Draft

This source is retained for audit history and is excluded from the production reading path. The corrections below govern its interpretation; the original wording is preserved separately.

The integral identity below is valid for a finite sum of integrable vector functions in a common coordinate representation. To interpret those functions as first variations of a nonlinear flow, differentiate a smooth family of solutions around one nominal state/input trajectory. Every variation then uses the same linear differential operator. Superposition also adds their initial variations.

The resulting endpoint sensitivity is exact as a derivative. It is not the finite difference between separately controlled nonlinear trajectories, and it does not assign unique fractions of biological causation. On a manifold, use a common chart or explicitly defined transport before adding vectors at different points. See [first variations and state transition](../../../tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-2-dynamics.html).

## 1. Introduction

This series extends the tangent-hyperplane framework by examining what
integrates when infinitesimal superposition holds exactly.

We show that while causes do not add globally, *variations* do, and that
this additivity is preserved under integration by linear transport.

## 2. Linearity of the Integral

If infinitesimal variations satisfy

$$
\delta \dot{x}(t) = \sum_i \delta \dot{x}_i(t),
$$

then by linearity of integration,

$$
\int_{t_0}^{t_1} \delta \dot{x}(t)\,dt
= \sum_i \int_{t_0}^{t_1} \delta \dot{x}_i(t)\,dt.
$$

This identity is exact.

## 3. Endpoint Interpretation

The integral corresponds to the net state variation:

$$
\delta x(t_1) - \delta x(t_0).
$$

Thus, what superposes globally is variation between endpoints, not
individual causal trajectories.

:::
